note: BUG#17 — Pizzas::Order.Purchase declares no `to` attribute of its own; its receiver is addressed the ordinary legacy way (a flat `name` key) and its only required facts are `amount`/`customer_name` (sets). A fuzzer-corrupted step can still offer a real, non-null `to:` (here a valid aggregate identity, so routing itself succeeds) ALONGSIDE those flat facts, with no `with:` key at all. Ruby's `Routing.payload` gates its facts source on `with:` alone (`return legacy unless with`) — whether `to:` is present, absent, null, or a real value never enters that decision — so `legacy` (the flat args minus `to`/`with`) still reaches Purchase's own validation, and Purchase succeeds (PizzaPurchased, `status` → "sold"). `CommandInvocation::from_json` (rust/src/kernel/routing.rs) used to conflate the two: any non-null `to` took the "explicit routing" branch, which defaulted `facts` to `with`'s own value — an EMPTY object, since `with:` was never offered — silently dropping `amount`/`customer_name`/`name` and refusing AbsentArgument for a fact Ruby never even had to check. Confirmed live pre-fix: this exact sequence refused `Pizzas::Order.Purchase was not given amount — it takes amount, customer_name` against the compiled Rust binary while Ruby succeeded.
